title: What are the blue region and the square?
description: Three identical squares are placed in an L shape, with a red triangle and a blue triangle on them. The red triangle equals one whole square, the blue triangle is a quarter of a square, and these give the blue area and the area of each square.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the base and the height of a triangle off the sides of identical squares, then use half of base times height. Watch for students who forget that the red height is two sides, not one.

video_script.why: The child applies the half of base times height method of the solved examples, reading the base and height off the sides of identical squares.
video_script.substitution: Find the base and the height of each triangle in sides of a square, then take half of base times height.
video_script.anchor: the book's three identical squares ABCD, BCEF and BFGH with the red triangle DCH and the blue triangle left of the line DH
video_script.payoff_line: Each square is one hundred forty four square units

final_answer.spoken: the blue region is twelve point two five square units, and each square is one hundred forty four square units

video_script.fraction_reading: a quarter and five quarters are said as words
never_show: the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: squares ABCD and BCEF sit side by side and BFGH sits on top of BCEF, so H is directly above B, a side length s above B
red triangle DCH: base DC = s and height CH = CB + BH = 2s, so area = 1/2 × s × 2s = s², one whole square
the line DH climbs 2s for a run of s, so it climbs s (the height of ABCD) after a run of s/2, and meets AB at its midpoint
blue triangle: legs s and s/2, area = 1/2 × s × s/2 = s²/4, one quarter of a square
(ii) blue + red = s² + s²/4 = 5s²/4 = 180, so s²/4 = 36 and s² = 144 sq. units (side 12)
video_script.design: One picture all video. The triangles are measured in sides of a square, so the red is one square and the blue is a quarter of a square.
open_questions: The figure is not in the extracted book text, so the red and blue regions follow the worklist: red is triangle DCH and blue is the part of ABCD to the left of DH.

<bookmark mark='areas'/>In the first picture, red is forty nine square units.
In the second, blue and red together are one hundred eighty.

Then we find the area of each square in the second.

beats.on_screen: Red triangle DCH: base DC = s, height CH = 2s; area = 1/2 × s × 2s = s², one whole square = 49

marks.tri: the red triangle D C H is outlined with DC = s marked
marks.area: 1/2 × s × 2s = s² is written and the red triangle is shown as one whole square

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step one, take the red triangle D C H. Its base D C is one side of a square.
<bookmark mark='ht'/>Its height C H is two sides, because C B and B H are both sides.
<bookmark mark='area'/>Half of one side times two sides is one whole square.
The red area equals one square, forty nine square units.

beats.on_screen: line DH climbs 2s for a run of s; after a run of s/2 it has climbed s, so it meets AB at its midpoint

marks.climb: the line D H is traced with its climb of two sides over one side across

narration: <bookmark mark='climb'/>Step two, look at the line D H. It climbs two sides for every one side across.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>It climbs one side, the height of the left square, after half a side across.
It meets eigh B at its middle.

beats.on_screen: Blue triangle: legs s and s/2; area = 1/2 × s × s/2 = s²/4; blue = 49 ÷ 4 = 12.25

marks.legs: the blue triangle shows one side going up and half a side across
marks.quarter: 1/2 × s × s/2 = s²/4 is written, one quarter of a square

narration: <bookmark mark='legs'/>Step three, the blue triangle has one side going up and half a side across.
<bookmark mark='quarter'/>Half of one side times half a side is a quarter of a square.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Divide forty nine by four to get twelve point two five.

beats.on_screen: (ii) blue + red = 1 square + 1/4 square = 5/4 of a square = 180; 1/4 of a square = 180 ÷ 5 = 36; a square = 36 × 4 = 144; check: 144 + 36 = 180

marks.tog: blue + red = 1 square + 1/4 square is written

narration: <bookmark mark='tog'/>Step four, blue and red together make one square and a quarter of a square.
<bookmark mark='five'/>That is five quarters of a square, and it equals one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>One quarter is one hundred eighty divided by five, which is thirty six.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>Four quarters make a whole square, so thirty six times four gives one hundred forty four.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check, one hundred forty four plus thirty six is one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The blue region is twelve point two five square units.
Each square is one hundred forty four square units.
